children: US spot Bitcoin ETFs just pulled in nearly $1 billion in a single trading day, marking the largest daily inflow these products have seen in roughly a year. The September 21 haul of $998.95 million landed as Bitcoin's price briefly punched above $87,000, its highest level since January, putting the average holder back in the green after months of sideways churn.
For context, this was the ninth-largest daily inflow since spot Bitcoin ETFs launched on January 11, 2024. The last time the number got this big was early October 2025.

BlackRock's IBIT dominated the day with $381 million in net inflows. ARK 21Shares' ARKB came in second at roughly $289 million. Fidelity's FBTC rounded out the top three with approximately $239 million. Together, those three funds accounted for more than 90% of the day's total.

Bitcoin's intraday push above $87,000 was the catalyst that flipped a meaningful chunk of holders back into profit. The price has since pulled back to the $85,000 to $86,000 range, but even that level represents a quarterly gain of about 44%.

It's worth noting that these inflows aren't happening in isolation. August 2026 saw $3.52 billion flow into Bitcoin ETFs across the entire month. September's month-to-date total has already reached $1.31 billion, and we're not even through the month yet.
Spot Ether ETFs also had a strong day, attracting approximately $270 million in inflows on September 21.

The $998.95 million day also serves as a reminder of how much the ETF wrapper has changed Bitcoin's investor base. Before January 2024, getting institutional exposure to Bitcoin required navigating custody arrangements, compliance hurdles, and risk frameworks that many traditional asset managers simply weren't set up for. Now it's a ticker symbol in a brokerage account.

title: Bitcoin ETFs attract nearly $1B in a day as holders return to profit
